partial_case.facts: The resident and her partner live in a 2-bedroom ground floor flat in a high-rise building. In February 2024 the landlord sent the resident notice of her new rent and service charges for the upcoming year. She queried the new charges in March 2024. On 12 March 2024 the resident submitted a complaint form to the landlord raising concerns about the level of service charge increase, lack of gardening since 2022, and the landlord's failure to investigate littering on the estate. She also objected to paying for lift maintenance (as she lived on the ground floor), the communal laundry (which she did not use) and the heating system (which she said ran year-round due to poor maintenance). On 2 April 2024 the resident chased a response to her concerns. She added that the landlord had refused to give her a paper complaint form when she had first requested one. On 16 April 2024 the landlord met with the resident and noted she was unhappy with the lack of response to her complaint. This included ASB concerns relating to items being thrown out of the windows by other residents. On 26 April 2024 the landlord acknowledged the complaint and said it had referred the resident's ASB concerns to its ASB team for investigation. On 29 April 2024 the landlord issued its stage 1 response. On 20 May 2024 the resident asked to escalate her complaint. She said she could not accept the landlord's stage 1 response because it had not provided any answers regarding the 106% increase in service charges. On 21 June 2024 the landlord issued its stage 2 response.

We have not seen evidence that this issue was raised as a formal complaint with the landlord and exhausted its internal complaints procedure.

partial_case.facts: The resident and her partner live in a 2-bedroom ground floor flat in a high-rise building. In February 2024 the landlord sent the resident notice of her new rent and service charges for the upcoming year, and she queried the new charges in March 2024. The complaint concerned service charge queries, reports of anti-social behaviour, and an associated complaint. On 12 March 2024 the resident submitted a complaint form raising concerns about the level of service charge increase, lack of gardening since 2022, littering on the estate, lift maintenance charges, the communal laundry, and the heating system. On 2 April 2024 the resident chased a response and said the landlord had refused to give her a paper complaint form when she first requested one. On 16 April 2024 the landlord met with the resident and noted concerns including ASB relating to items being thrown out of windows by other residents. On 26 April 2024 the landlord acknowledged the complaint and said it had referred the resident’s ASB concerns to its ASB team for investigation. On 29 April 2024 the landlord issued its stage 1 response. On 20 May 2024 the resident asked to escalate her complaint because the stage 1 response had not provided answers regarding the 106% increase in service charges. On 21 June 2024 the landlord issued its stage 2 response, acknowledged it had not fully addressed the complaint at stage 1, and explained the increase as due to a shortfall carried over from previous years. The resident referred the complaint to the Ombudsman because she was unhappy with the landlord’s response to her service charge queries, wanted to challenge the level of increase, and also raised concerns about gardening and cleaning, ASB, and complaint responses.

orders: £350 compensation, comprising £300 for service charge query handling and £50 for complaint handling
Follow-up actions from the stage 2 response
Action plan for monitoring cleaning and gardening
Reminder to customer-facing staff about logging complaints and the Complaints Handling Code
